en: 6. The Question on the Mooring-Post “Venerable Nāgasena, as for what you say—that two qualities of a mooring-post should be adopted—what are those two qualities that should be adopted?

“Just as, O King, a mooring-post, in the great ocean where the surface of the water is agitated and stirred by a multitude of waves, anchors and steadies a ship, not allowing it to be carried away in this direction or that;”

In the same way, Great King, the yogin practicing yoga must fix his mind upon the great net of the smoke of lust, hatred, and delusion, amidst the violent impact of vast and mighty thoughts; he must not allow it to be carried away toward the cardinal or intermediate directions.
This, Great King, is the first factor to be grasped from the mooring of a ship.
Furthermore, Great King, the mooring of a ship does not float or sink; even in water a hundred cubits deep, it moors the ship and brings it to a standstill.

In the same way, great king, a practitioner of yoga should not be carried away even by the highest gain, fame, honor, reverence, salutation, worship, or veneration; rather, he should fix his mind on nothing more than the mere maintenance of the body.
This, great king, is the second quality to be adopted from the mooring of a ship.
And this, great king, was said by the Elder Sāriputta, the General of the Dhamma:
"Just as a boat in the ocean neither floats nor sinks,
so too in gain and honor..."
This is the sixth question concerning the oar used for mooring a boat.
